newsitem.title: DUBAI: GOLF-OLAZABAL PUTTER HELPS HOSPITAL TO MOVE TWO AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-OLAZABAL PUTTER HELPS HOSPITAL TO MOVE TWO AHEAD.

text.p: Unheralded Spaniard Domingo Hospital, using a putter given to him by Jose Maria Olazabal, fashioned a three-under-par 69 to take a two-shot halfway lead in the Dubai Desert Classic on Friday.
Then he insisted that he could not win the tournament because he lacked vital experience.

"I don't think I can do it because there are a lot of mental things that I'll go through and I don't know how I'll react because I have not been there before," said Hospital, who has never led at the halfway stage of a tour event.
Olazabal gave his comeback from injury a major boost by doing enough to survive the halfway cut despite a triple bogey eight midway through his second round of 74.
The 38-year-old Hospital, a tour player for just four years, scrambled through some bad driving by taking just 27 putts after switching on Tuesday to the club given to him two years ago by Olazabal.
"I brought it with me just to practise with in my hotel room but after Monday when I putted badly with my old club I decided to use it," he said.
He needed only 28 putts on Thursday, one less in the second round. "That's why I'm here talking to you," said the Spaniard after compiling a 36-hole total of 134, 10 under par.

The big-name challengers are lining up behind him. Ian Woosnam and Bernhard Langer, perennial Ryder Cup stalwarts, share second place on eight under after respective rounds of 67, the best score on a windy day, and 70.
Titleholder Colin Montgomerie is another shot back after a 72 with world number one Greg Norman in a group on five under par after a 68.

Olazabal, out of action for 18 months with chronic foot problems, drove badly at the 18th hole, his ninth, but was unlucky to run up an eight. Yet he battled back for a 74 that left him inside the projected cutoff of one over par.
"I'm happy just to be playing at the weekend," he said.
Compatriot Seve Ballesteros, however, soared to an 84 and the 1992 winner here missed the halfway cut for the third time in his three events this year.
